connectivity_tips.tip: eSIMs are the easiest connectivity option — no physical SIM required and can be activated before departure via QR code. Popular providers include Airalo, Nomad, and Holafly, with Europe-wide coverage including France and Switzerland.

Local SIM card providers in Switzerland include Swisscom (best overall coverage including mountains), Sunrise (reliable alternative), and Salt (budget-friendly option). Available at Zurich HB Station, Lucerne Station, airports, and official stores. Passport mandatory for SIM registration.
Strong connectivity on most train routes; brief signal drops in tunnels are normal.
Excellent mobile coverage even in mountain regions like Jungfraujoch, Titlis, and Interlaken.
Wi-Fi is widely available in hotels, cafés, and stations throughout France and Switzerland.

eSIM is recommended for convenience — activate before leaving India. Popular providers include Airalo, Nomad, and Holafly. Purchase online, scan QR code, and activate instantly with no physical SIM needed. Choose a Europe-wide plan if traveling beyond Switzerland.

Local Swiss SIM cards are reliable with excellent coverage across cities and mountains. Top providers: Swisscom (best coverage), Sunrise, and Salt. Available at Zurich Airport, Zurich HB, convenience stores, and telecom shops. Passport required for registration.

International roaming from India is the most effortless option but usually more expensive. Popular providers: Airtel International Roaming and Jio International Packs. Check data limits carefully as plans can be costly.
Download Google Maps offline for all destinations before traveling.
Use the SBB Mobile App for real-time train schedules, live platform numbers, delays, train connections, and boat, tram, and bus schedules. Available on iOS App Store and Google Play Store.
Expect brief signal drops in tunnels and remote alpine areas.
Best setup: One Europe-wide SIM or eSIM with WiFi backup strategy. Switzerland and Italy are both supported by EU roaming providers via Italy-based SIMs or global eSIMs.

eSIM is most recommended. Providers include Airalo (Europe eSIM), Holafly (Unlimited data plans), and Nomad eSIM (Flexible regional packs). Offers instant activation, works immediately upon landing, keeps primary SIM active for OTPs, and no risk of losing physical SIM.
Suggested eSIM plan: 10–20 GB for light usage (maps, WhatsApp, bookings) or unlimited plan for heavy navigation and uploads.

Local SIM in Switzerland available at Zurich Airport kiosks, Geneva Airport shops, and Swisscom/Sunrise stores. Best providers: Swisscom (best coverage, premium), Sunrise (good value), Salt Mobile (budget). Typical cost: CHF 20–60 depending on data package. Recommended plan: 5–10 GB.

Download offline maps of Switzerland (entire region) and Northern + Central Italy before travelling. Upload photos only on WiFi when possible. Avoid streaming during train rides unless on unlimited plan. Turn off background app refresh for non-essential apps.
Essential apps: Trenitalia App and Italo Treno App for Italy trains; SBB Mobile for Switzerland trains; Google Maps and Maps.me for navigation; WhatsApp for communication.

An eSIM is the easiest and most convenient option for multi-country Europe trips. Recommended providers: Airalo, Holafly, Nomad. Works across multiple European countries with no physical SIM swapping required.

Local SIM cards available from Swisscom, Sunrise, and Salt. Purchase at Zurich/Lucerne stations or airport kiosks. Passport required. Excellent mountain and train route connectivity. Note: Switzerland is not fully covered under some EU roaming plans — check before purchasing.
